- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥ 15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then allow gradual decay.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (especially after 3+ days), model underreacts; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days to align with sentiment shift.
- Model consistently underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d avg, reduce by 5–8% to align with historical mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model over-optimistically assumes continuation; reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–10 days unless confirmed by event-driven catalysts.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize “sell-off” sentiment; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days if sentiment remains negative.
